cards.title: Self-Supervised Confidence Fine-Tuning Cuts Reasoning Tokens by 25% Without Length Penalties
cards.why_it_matters: If you work with long-chain-of-thought models, this shows a training-signal shortcut — only 600 problems, no RL length penalties — that competes with explicit efficiency objectives.
cards.summary: Fine-tuning reasoning models (Gemma, Qwen, Nemotron, GPT-OSS) to predict their own mid-trajectory confidence reduces generated tokens by up to 25% at matched accuracy on math, science, and coding benchmarks. No early-stopping or confidence elicitation is used at inference. The efficiency gain emerges as a side-effect of metacognitive supervision, not direct length optimization.

cards.title: Black-Box Post-Processing Algorithms Align Generative AI Output Attribute Distributions to User Targets
cards.why_it_matters: Fairness and synthetic-data use cases often require distributional control without model access; query-optimal post-processing algorithms are a practical tool for ML deployment pipelines.
cards.summary: For black-box generative models, the paper develops algorithms that post-process outputs so their joint attribute distribution matches a user-specified target, minimizing expected query count. Both exact and approximate alignment are covered, with optimality proved as requested outputs grow. Experiments on text-to-image and geocoded persona generation validate improvements over prompting-based interventions.

cards.title: Gap-Free Differentially Private PCA Algorithm for Gaussian Data
cards.why_it_matters: Differential privacy for PCA has long required eigenvalue gap assumptions; a gap-free result is a meaningful theoretical advance for privacy-preserving ML pipelines.
cards.summary: The paper presents a differentially private PCA algorithm that removes the eigenvalue gap assumption previously required, specifically for Gaussian-distributed data. Details on error rates and mechanisms are not provided in the abstract beyond this core claim.

cards.title: First-Order Stationarity Theory for Reverse Diffusion Samplers Parallels Nonconvex Optimization
cards.why_it_matters: Understanding diffusion sampling through an optimization lens gives researchers sharper convergence guarantees and a principled framework for analyzing discretized samplers.
cards.summary: SDE-based reverse diffusions of overdamped and underdamped Langevin processes contract relative Fisher divergences at explicit exponential rates when the forward process's stationary potential is strongly convex — a condition on the noising process, not the data. Discretization analysis yields averaged first-order stationarity bounds analogous to averaged gradient-norm guarantees in nonconvex optimization, guaranteeing score consistency rather than global mode weights.

cards.title: Measurement-Based Uncomputation Framework Trades Probabilistic Success for Quantum Circuit Spacetime Cost
cards.why_it_matters: Reducing uncomputation overhead is critical for early fault-tolerant quantum algorithms; this algebraic framework offers structured trade-offs directly relevant to quantum ML and near-term quantum computing.
cards.summary: The paper frames measurement-based uncomputation (MBU) via quantum error correction: measurements on garbage registers induce phase errors whose syndrome determines success probability. Post-selected MBU eliminates the uncomputation oracle at probabilistic cost governed by the affine rank of the garbage support, shown to be small in the HHL algorithm example. A structural condition allows reuse of the original oracle for phase correction, interpolating between post-selected, partial, and deterministic MBU.
